<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** People can pick their name and office managers can manage rooms, but nobody can book a room. This is loose work outside the initiative tree (user, 2026-11-12), built exactly as asked rather than as `epic-find-and-book`.

**Approach:** Add a `bookings` module (web, service, store) and a migration for `bookings` and `booking_attendees`. In it, a Rooms page lists the free rooms for a chosen date, start time and length, with your own office first and a minimum-capacity filter. You book from the list with a title and attendees picked from the people list. A booking details page shows room, time, title and organiser to anyone, shows attendees only to the organiser, the attendees and the room's office managers, and lets the organiser cancel. Overlapping bookings, bookings of closed rooms, bookings in the past and bookings more than 90 days ahead are refused, even when two people book the same slot at once. Closing a room deletes its future bookings.

</frozen-after-approval>

## Implementation Notes

Oneshot route, pinned by the workflow. The user settled every scope question at the step-01 checkpoint (commit pending files, branch `room-booking`, build what was asked, attendees per AD-8). The architecture spine (AD-1 to AD-13) already fixes the module shape, so most of the remaining decisions are written down here:

- Layout follows the spine: `roombooker/bookings/{store,service,web}.py`, `roombooker/core/time.py` (the only Europe/London conversion, plus Jinja filters `14:00` and `Tue 17 Nov`), templates under `templates/bookings/`, migration `0003_bookings.py`.
- AD-4: `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` triggers on `bookings` refuse overlaps (half-open) and closed rooms with `RAISE(ABORT, 'booking_conflict' | 'room_closed')`. Writes run under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and the service maps each abort to `BookingConflict`/`RoomClosed` (409). `CHECK (end_at > start_at)`. `booking_attendees` cascades on delete (AD-13). A threaded concurrency test proves the trigger.
- AD-5: UTC text `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z`. The service checks 15-minute alignment, a length of 15 to 240 minutes, a start no earlier than now and no more than 90 days after now, and a title of 1 to 100 characters. Attendees must be active people; the organiser is never stored as an attendee. Clock times that don't exist in the UK (the spring-forward gap) are refused in the web layer.
- Closing cascades: AD-1 forbids `rooms.service` → `bookings`. An `AFTER UPDATE OF is_closed` trigger on `rooms` deletes bookings whose `start_at` is later than now. It runs in the close transaction, and a booking already in progress stays. The close confirmation says future bookings will be cancelled. This is recorded as an ADR in `docs/decisions/`.
- Rooms page `/rooms`: the search form is a full GET that also works with htmx. It shows free open rooms grouped by office (own office first, then by name), each with a Book link, and lists "Booked at this time" (title, organiser, link to details) and "Your upcoming bookings" so the organiser can reach Cancel. `/` sends non-managers to `/rooms`, and the top bar gains a Rooms tab for everyone.
- Booking form `/bookings/new?room&date&start&length`: the title defaults to "{Name}'s meeting". Attendees are added by htmx type-ahead from `people.service.search_active_people`, held as hidden `attendee_id` inputs; without JS a GET search reloads the form. A refusal keeps the title and attendees. `POST /bookings` redirects to `/bookings/{id}`, and `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel` asks for confirmation first (GET `/bookings/{id}/cancel`).
- Test policy: one test per distinct behaviour, and no test repeats what another already proves.

Built:
- New: `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py`, `roombooker/core/time.py`, `roombooker/bookings/{store,service,web}.py`, `templates/bookings/{rooms,new,details,_item}.html`, `docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md`, `tests/test_bookings.py`, `tests/e2e/test_book_a_room.py`.
- Changed: `people.service`/`store` (`names`, which includes inactive people, and `office_names`); `rooms.service`/`store` (`all_rooms`, `find_room`); `app.py` (router, `clock`/`day` filters); `/` now sends non-managers to `/rooms` (`people/landing.html` removed); top bar has a Rooms tab for everyone; close confirmation mentions cancelled bookings; README; CSS.
- Existing tests updated for the new landing, the tab bar and the close wording.
- `bookings.web` reaches rooms and people only through `bookings.service` (`room_to_book`, `attendee_choices`), per AD-1.
- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` works because Python's sqlite3 in legacy transaction mode opens no transaction for reads. `store.begin_immediate` commits the session, then issues it. A scratch check confirmed a second connection is locked out until rollback.
- The 90-day limit is measured from now (start ≤ now + 90 days), not by UK calendar date. Cancelling a booking that has already ended is refused. Managers cancel only their own bookings (as asked), not others' in their office.
- One full-suite run of seven had a single failure that never reproduced. Six later full runs passed, and the failure's name was not captured. Treat it as a possible flaky test.

# Company Room Booking

## Description

One web app where anyone in the company finds a free meeting room in London, Manchester or Leeds and books it, with double bookings made impossible. It replaces the three per-office spreadsheets and rooms named in calendar invites, which grew unworkable this year as the company reached three offices and more people came back in. Release one has no accounts and no outside calendars: people pick their name, book, and see their bookings in a built-in calendar; office managers keep their office's rooms current. Inputs: the final brief, PRD and UX (References).

## Outcome

About 300 staff and their office managers find and book rooms in one trusted place instead of three spreadsheets, shown by PRD SM-1 to SM-3 and watched by the SM-4 stop signal and the SM-5 counter-metric.

## Requirements

- R1 (FR-1): A person picks their name from the loaded people and then uses the app as that person, with their name shown throughout.
- R2 (FR-2): A person can switch to another name at any time; the picked name is remembered on that device until they switch.
- R3 (FR-3): An office manager adds a room to their office, with at least a name and a capacity.
- R4 (FR-4): An office manager edits a room in their office.
- R5 (FR-5, RULE-5): An office manager closes and reopens a room in their office; a closed room shows as closed and cannot be booked.
- R6 (FR-6): A person chooses an office, a date, a start time and a length and sees which of that office's rooms are free, on a laptop and on a phone, for any time, not only from now; their home office is shown first and any office can be chosen.
- R7 (FR-7, UJ-1): A person books a free room by giving a start time, a length from 15 minutes to 4 hours, a title and attendees from the loaded people; they become its organiser, and the booking shows in their calendar and every attendee's.
- R8 (FR-8): Any booking, or change to a booking, that would overlap another booking of the same room is refused, and the person is told why.
- R9 (FR-9): The organiser changes a booking's room, start time, length, title or attendees under the same rules as a new booking.
- R10 (FR-10): An office manager changes any booking of a room in their office under the same rules as R9.
- R11 (FR-11): The organiser, or an office manager of the room's office, cancels a booking, and the room shows as free to everyone at once.
- R12 (FR-12): A person sees their own bookings, both those they organise and those they attend, in a built-in calendar by day and by week.
- R13 (FR-13): From their calendar a person opens one of their bookings and changes or cancels it when RULE-3 allows.
- R14 (FR-14): A person moves their calendar to the previous or next day or week.
- R15 (EXPERIENCE Booking Visibility): Everyone sees a booking's room, time, title and organiser; its attendees are shown only to the organiser, the attendees and office managers of the room's office.
- R16 (EXPERIENCE Interaction Primitives): A person books a free room in three taps or fewer, with no typing required.

## Constraints

- RULE-1, PRD Decisions: Two bookings of the same room never overlap in time; there is no override, for office managers either.
- RULE-2: A booking lasts from 15 minutes to 4 hours; start times and lengths move in 15-minute steps.
- RULE-3: Only a booking's organiser and the office managers of the room's office may change or cancel it.
- RULE-4: Only office managers may add, edit, close or reopen rooms, and only in their own office, which is their home office.
- RULE-6: No accounts or passwords in release one; anyone can pick anyone's name, and every booking shows its organiser.
- RULE-7: Built with Python, FastAPI and SQLite; the user's computer is for building and testing, and where it runs for the company is decided in the architecture.
- RULE-8: Free rooms for a given office and time are visible in under 10 seconds from opening the app.
- RULE-9: Every feature works in a browser on a laptop and on a phone.
- PRD Quality and constraints: One time zone, UK time, for all three offices.
- PRD Decisions, Rollout: Before go-live office managers check their office's rooms are in the app and correct; at go-live the spreadsheets are frozen and organisers re-enter their own future bookings, so no spreadsheet import is built.
- User, 2026-11-12: Offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks load from a seed file while building; HR supplies the real list before go-live, and it loads the same way.

## Done when

# Company Room Booking

## Description

One web app where anyone in the company finds a free meeting room in London, Manchester or Leeds and books it, with double bookings made impossible. It replaces the three per-office spreadsheets and rooms named in calendar invites, which grew unworkable this year as the company reached three offices and more people came back in. Release one has no accounts and no outside calendars: people pick their name, book, and see their bookings in a built-in calendar; office managers keep their office's rooms current. Inputs: the final brief, PRD and UX (References).

## Outcome

About 300 staff and their office managers find and book rooms in one trusted place instead of three spreadsheets, shown by PRD SM-1 to SM-3 and watched by the SM-4 stop signal and the SM-5 counter-metric.

## Requirements

- R1 (FR-1): A person picks their name from the loaded people and then uses the app as that person, with their name shown throughout.
- R2 (FR-2): A person can switch to another name at any time; the picked name is remembered on that device until they switch.
- R3 (FR-3): An office manager adds a room to their office, with at least a name and a capacity.
- R4 (FR-4): An office manager edits a room in their office.
- R5 (FR-5, RULE-5): An office manager closes and reopens a room in their office; a closed room shows as closed and cannot be booked.
- R6 (FR-6): A person chooses an office, a date, a start time and a length and sees which of that office's rooms are free, on a laptop and on a phone, for any time, not only from now; their home office is shown first and any office can be chosen.
- R7 (FR-7, UJ-1): A person books a free room by giving a start time, a length from 15 minutes to 4 hours, a title and attendees from the loaded people; they become its organiser, and the booking shows in their calendar and every attendee's.
- R8 (FR-8): Any booking, or change to a booking, that would overlap another booking of the same room is refused, and the person is told why.
- R9 (FR-9): The organiser changes a booking's room, start time, length, title or attendees under the same rules as a new booking.
- R10 (FR-10): An office manager changes any booking of a room in their office under the same rules as R9.
- R11 (FR-11): The organiser, or an office manager of the room's office, cancels a booking, and the room shows as free to everyone at once.
- R12 (FR-12): A person sees their own bookings, both those they organise and those they attend, in a built-in calendar by day and by week.
- R13 (FR-13): From their calendar a person opens one of their bookings and changes or cancels it when RULE-3 allows.
- R14 (FR-14): A person moves their calendar to the previous or next day or week.
- R15 (EXPERIENCE Booking Visibility): Everyone sees a booking's room, time, title and organiser; its attendees are shown only to the organiser, the attendees and office managers of the room's office.
- R16 (EXPERIENCE Interaction Primitives): A person books a free room in three taps or fewer, with no typing required.

## Constraints

- RULE-1, PRD Decisions: Two bookings of the same room never overlap in time; there is no override, for office managers either.
- RULE-2: A booking lasts from 15 minutes to 4 hours; start times and lengths move in 15-minute steps.
- RULE-3: Only a booking's organiser and the office managers of the room's office may change or cancel it.
- RULE-4: Only office managers may add, edit, close or reopen rooms, and only in their own office, which is their home office.
- RULE-6: No accounts or passwords in release one; anyone can pick anyone's name, and every booking shows its organiser.
- RULE-7: Built with Python, FastAPI and SQLite; the user's computer is for building and testing, and where it runs for the company is decided in the architecture.
- RULE-8: Free rooms for a given office and time are visible in under 10 seconds from opening the app.
- RULE-9: Every feature works in a browser on a laptop and on a phone.
- PRD Quality and constraints: One time zone, UK time, for all three offices.
- PRD Decisions, Rollout: Before go-live office managers check their office's rooms are in the app and correct; at go-live the spreadsheets are frozen and organisers re-enter their own future bookings, so no spreadsheet import is built.
- User, 2026-11-12: Offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks load from a seed file while building; HR supplies the real list before go-live, and it loads the same way.

"""Rooms (find a free room), the booking form, booking details and cancelling. Calls `bookings.service` only (AD-1), and `core.time` for UK time (AD-5). Every route works on a full page load; htmx only narrows the swap with `hx-select` (AD-2). Writes are form POSTs with redirect-after-post. """ from datetime import datetime, timedelta from typing import Annotated from urllib.parse import urlencode from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, Query, Request from fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse, Response from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from roombooker.bookings import service from roombooker.bookings.service import ( BookingConflict, InvalidBooking, RoomClosed, ) from roombooker.core import time as uk from roombooker.core.db import get_session from roombooker.core.identity import CurrentPerson from roombooker.people.service import Person router = APIRouter() DbSession = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)] FormText = Annotated[str, Form()] DEFAULT_LENGTH = 30 START_OPTIONS = [f"{h:02d}:{m:02d}" for h in range(24) for m in range(0, 60, 15)] LENGTH_OPTIONS = [ (str(minutes), uk.length_label(minutes)) for minutes in range(service.LENGTH_MIN, service.LENGTH_MAX + 1, service.STEP_MINUTES) ] NEEDS_DATE = "Pick a date." NEEDS_START = "Pick a start time." SKIPPED_TIME = "The clocks go forward then, so that time does not exist. Pick another." BAD_CAPACITY = "People must be a whole number, or blank for any size." NOTICES = {"cancelled": "Booking cancelled."} def _render(request: Request, template: str, status_code: int = 200, **context) -> Response: response = request.app.state.templates.TemplateResponse( request, template, context, status_code=status_code ) response.headers["Vary"] = "HX-Request" return response def _whole(text: str, digits: int = 4) -> int | None: text = text.strip() return int(text) if text.isascii() and text.isdigit() and len(text) <= digits else None def _slot(date_text: str, start_text: str, length_text: str) -> tuple[datetime, int]: """The UTC start and length in minutes of a UK date, clock time and length.""" day = uk.parse_date(date_text) if day is None: raise InvalidBooking(NEEDS_DATE) start_clock = uk.parse_clock(start_text) if start_clock is None: raise InvalidBooking(NEEDS_START) length = _whole(length_text) if length is None: raise InvalidBooking(service.BAD_LENGTH) start_at = uk.uk_to_utc(day, start_clock) if start_at is None: raise InvalidBooking(SKIPPED_TIME) return start_at, length def _slot_text(start_at: datetime, length: int) -> str: end_at = start_at + timedelta(minutes=length) return f"{uk.day(start_at)}, {uk.clock(start_at)}–{uk.clock(end_at)}" def _attendee_ids(values: list[str]) -> list[int]: return [i for i in (_whole(v, 18) for v in values) if i is not None] @router.api_route("/rooms", methods=["GET", "HEAD"]) def rooms( request: Request, session: DbSession, person: CurrentPerson, date: str = "", start: str = "", length: str = "", capacity: str = "", notice: str = "", ) -> Response: if not date and not start: first = uk.next_quarter_hour(uk.uk_now()) date, start = first.date().isoformat(), first.strftime("%H:%M") length = length or str(DEFAULT_LENGTH) context = { "person": person, "values": {"date": date, "start": start, "length": length, "capacity": capacity}, "start_options": START_OPTIONS, "length_options": LENGTH_OPTIONS, "notice": NOTICES.get(notice), "error": None, "groups": [], "in_slot": [], "slot_text": None, "book_query": None, "upcoming": service.upcoming_bookings(session, person), } status_code = 200 try: start_at, minutes = _slot(date, start, length) min_capacity = _whole(capacity) if capacity.strip() else 1 if min_capacity is None: raise InvalidBooking(BAD_CAPACITY) context["groups"] = service.free_rooms(session, person, start_at, minutes, min_capacity) context["in_slot"] = service.bookings_in_slot(session, person, start_at, minutes) context["slot_text"] = _slot_text(start_at, minutes) context["book_query"] = urlencode({"date": date, "start": start, "length": length}) except InvalidBooking as exc: context["error"] = exc.message status_code = exc.status_code return _render(request, "bookings/rooms.html", status_code, # Each person sees their own bookings by day and week

## Description

A person sees every booking they organise or attend in a built-in calendar, by day and by week, moves between days and weeks, and opens a booking to change or cancel it. It reuses epic-offices-and-rooms' shell and epic-find-and-book's date switcher and booking details panel, so it adds the calendar views, not new booking rules.

## Outcome

Each person trusts the app as their only room calendar, which retires the spreadsheets (initiative SM-3).

## Done when

- On the deployed app, a person's day and week views show every booking they organise and every one they attend, including bookings others added them to.
- A person moves to the previous or next day or week.
- Opening a booking from the calendar allows change or cancel only under RULE-3, and the calendar updates at once.
- Integrated verification on the deployed app passes, on laptop and phone.

## Boundaries

- Not here: making, changing or cancelling bookings and their rules; epic-find-and-book, reused through its booking details panel.
- R7 here is its calendar side only: a booking showing in the organiser's and every attendee's calendar.
- Not here: outside calendars or notifications (initiative Boundaries).

## References

- parent — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/initiative-company-room-booking.md, section Requirements (R7, R12 to R14) and Constraints
- experience — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/ux-company-room-booking/EXPERIENCE.md, My bookings, My bookings calendar, Responsive & Platform
- design — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/ux-company-room-booking/DESIGN.md
- architecture — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking.md, AD-3, AD-5, AD-7, AD-8, AD-13

# Each person sees their own bookings by day and week

## Description

A person sees every booking they organise or attend in a built-in calendar, by day and by week, moves between days and weeks, and opens a booking to change or cancel it. It reuses epic-offices-and-rooms' shell and epic-find-and-book's date switcher and booking details panel, so it adds the calendar views, not new booking rules.

## Outcome

Each person trusts the app as their only room calendar, which retires the spreadsheets (initiative SM-3).

## Done when

- On the deployed app, a person's day and week views show every booking they organise and every one they attend, including bookings others added them to.
- A person moves to the previous or next day or week.
- Opening a booking from the calendar allows change or cancel only under RULE-3, and the calendar updates at once.
- Integrated verification on the deployed app passes, on laptop and phone.

## Boundaries

- Not here: making, changing or cancelling bookings and their rules; epic-find-and-book, reused through its booking details panel.
- R7 here is its calendar side only: a booking showing in the organiser's and every attendee's calendar.
- Not here: outside calendars or notifications (initiative Boundaries).

97	## Brand & Style
98	
99	Company Room Booking is an internal tool, and it should look like one: the company's navy and white, plain surfaces, nothing decorative. Its whole job is to show, at a glance, which rooms are free and to get a person into one in three taps or fewer. The visual language serves that glance: white means free, navy means taken, and nothing else on the screen competes with those two. [ASSUMPTION: the posture "plain and tool-like" is inferred from "internal tool" and the company colors.]
100	
101	## Colors
102	
103	Two company colors, navy and white (user), and a small set of supporting tones. The navy hex is a placeholder until the company's exact navy is supplied; the supporting tones follow from it.
104	
105	- **Navy (`#1B2A4A`)** is the company color. Used for the top bar, primary buttons, the user's own bookings, and body text. Navy means "this is ours / act here".
106	- **White (`#FFFFFF`)** is the canvas and the color of a free slot. Free space is literally empty space.

## Brand & Style

Company Room Booking is an internal tool, and it should look like one: the company's navy and white, plain surfaces, nothing decorative. Its whole job is to show, at a glance, which rooms are free and to get a person into one in three taps or fewer. The visual language serves that glance: white means free, navy means taken, and nothing else on the screen competes with those two. [ASSUMPTION: the posture "plain and tool-like" is inferred from "internal tool" and the company colors.]

## Colors

Two company colors, navy and white (user), and a small set of supporting tones. The navy hex is a placeholder until the company's exact navy is supplied; the supporting tones follow from it.

- **Navy (`#1B2A4A`)** is the company color. Used for the top bar, primary buttons, the user's own bookings, and body text. Navy means "this is ours / act here".
- **White (`#FFFFFF`)** is the canvas and the color of a free slot. Free space is literally empty space.
- **Navy tint (`#E8ECF4`)** marks a slot booked by someone else: taken, but not yours.
- **Ink muted (`#5B6474`)** for secondary text: times, capacities, "free until" labels.
- **Border (`#D5DAE3`)** for grid lines, row outlines and input borders.
- **Closed (`#F2F3F5`)** for a closed room's row: visibly out of use, not an error.
- **Error (`#B42318`, on `#FDECEA`)** only for a refused booking or a failed save. [ASSUMPTION: an error red is added because refusals must stand out; it is the only non-navy hue.]

Avoid: any other brand hue, gradients, or using color alone to mean free, booked or closed (each always carries a text label; see EXPERIENCE.md Accessibility Floor).

## Typography

System font stack throughout [ASSUMPTION: no company font named]. Four roles: `title` (20px, screen headings), `body` (16px, default text and inputs; 16px also stops phones zooming into fields), `label` (14px semibold, room names, buttons, column heads), `meta` (14px, times and secondary detail). Nothing smaller than 14px.

## Layout & Spacing

A 4-based spacing scale (`{spacing.1}` to `{spacing.6}`). Every tappable element is at least `{spacing.touch-target}` (44px) tall.

- **Laptop (768px and wider):** full-width day grid, rooms as rows and time as columns, so all 10–15 rooms of an office fit on one screen without scrolling vertically.
- **Phone (under 768px):** a single column of room rows, `{spacing.4}` side margins.

Breakpoint behavior is in EXPERIENCE.md Responsive & Platform.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat. The only raised element is the booking sheet (a light shadow over a dimmed page). No shadows as decoration.

## Shapes

`{rounded.sm}` (4px) for slots in the grid and error messages; `{rounded.md}` (8px) for buttons, room rows and the booking sheet. No pills or circles. Focus rings follow each element's own shape.

## Components

- **Top bar:** `{colors.navy}` with white text: app name, the current person's name (tap to switch), and the navigation tabs.
- **Primary button:** navy fill, white text, `{rounded.md}`, at least 44px tall. One per screen or sheet: "Book", "Save", "Add room".
- **Secondary button:** white with a navy outline: "Cancel booking", "Close room", "Change".
- **Day grid slot:** four looks, each with a text label as well as color. *Free*: white with a hairline border. *Booked by someone else*: navy tint, showing title and organiser. *Mine* (I organise or attend): solid navy, white text. *Closed room*: grey row with the word "Closed".
- **Room row (phone):** white card with border: room name and capacity on the left; "Free until 15:30" in `meta`; a "Book" button on the right.
- **Booking sheet:** a white panel over the page: bottom sheet on phone, centred panel on laptop. Room, time and length prefilled; title and attendees editable; one primary "Book" button.
- **Error message:** error text on error tint, directly above the button it relates to.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep to navy, white and the listed supporting tones | Add a second brand color or decorative accents |
| Label every slot state in words as well as color | Rely on navy vs. white alone to say "booked" |
| Make every tap target at least 44px | Shrink rows to fit more on a phone |
| Use error red only for refusals and failed saves | Use red for closed rooms or past times |
| Keep the grid flat and dense on laptop | Add cards, shadows or icons to grid cells |

type: feature

baseline_revision: '2d594ea273897f1080a502a6f780ec3e5a4e06d6'
route: oneshot

  - '{project-root}/_bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** People can book rooms, but the only place they see their bookings is the "Your upcoming bookings" list on Rooms. That list shows only bookings they organise, not ones they were invited to, and they can't look at a given day or week. This is loose work outside the initiative tree (user, 2026-11-12), built as asked rather than as `epic-my-calendar`.

**Approach:** Add a My bookings page with a day view and a week view of every booking the current person organises or attends. Today is highlighted. Each booking shows its room, time and title and links to its details page. On a phone the same bookings show as a list.

</frozen-after-approval>

## Implementation Notes

Oneshot route, pinned by the workflow. The work is read-only (no new table, no write path, no rule change), so risk is low. The architecture spine already names the module (`calendar`, web and service, no store, AD-1/AD-3) and the route (`/my-bookings`). Decisions:

- `bookings.store.for_person(session, person_id, start, end)` finds bookings that overlap `[start, end)` where the person is the organiser or in `booking_attendees`, in start order. `bookings.service.bookings_for_person(session, viewer, start_at, end_at)` returns them as `BookingView`s through `_views` (AD-3, AD-8). `calendar.service.my_bookings` is the only thing `calendar.web` calls, and it calls only `bookings.service` (AD-1).
- UK time stays in `core.time` (AD-5): `uk_midnight(day) -> UTC datetime` (UK midnight always exists, so day bounds are correct across clock changes) and `week_start(day)` (Monday). `calendar.web` builds the list of days (1 or 7), asks for the UTC range from the first day's midnight to the midnight after the last day, and puts each booking under every UK day it overlaps.
- Route `GET /my-bookings?view=day|week&date=YYYY-MM-DD`. A missing or bad `view` means `day`; a missing or bad `date` means today in the UK. Week view always runs Monday to Sunday and contains `date`. Controls are plain links (a full page load, AD-2): Day / Week toggle (`aria-current`), Previous / Next (moves by one day or one week), and Today.
- Today: its day heading reads "Today" plus the date, has the class `is-today` and `aria-current="date"`, and is navy-tinted. The tint always comes with the word "Today", so colour is never the only signal (DESIGN).
- Each booking is a link to `/bookings/{id}` showing its time `10:00–11:00`, title, room and office, and an "Organiser" or "Attending" label (EXPERIENCE "My bookings calendar"). Bookings that have ended are still shown.
- Layout is one HTML structure: a `<section>` per day, each with a heading and a `<ul>` of bookings. At 768px and wider, week view puts the seven days side by side as a CSS grid of columns. Below 768px the days stack as day-headed lists, the phone layout EXPERIENCE gives. Day view is a single list at every width.
- Empty states: "No bookings today." / "No bookings on Tue 17 Nov." for a day; "No bookings this week." / "No bookings in the week of Mon 16 Nov." for a week. In week view an empty day shows "Nothing booked".
- Top bar: a "My bookings" tab for everyone, placed between Rooms and Manage rooms (EXPERIENCE navigation). The details page keeps "Back to rooms"; changing details and cancel navigation is out of scope.
- Test policy: one test per distinct behaviour, and no test may repeat what another test already proves.

Tasks:
- `roombooker/core/time.py` -- add `uk_midnight`, `week_start`.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py`, `service.py` -- add `for_person` / `bookings_for_person`.
- `roombooker/calendar/{__init__,service,web}.py`, `templates/calendar/my_bookings.html` -- the page; register the router in `app.py`.
- `templates/base.html` -- add the My bookings tab. `static/app.css` -- calendar styles.
- `tests/test_calendar.py` -- organised and attended bookings shown, other people's not; week runs Monday–Sunday and day bounds follow UK midnight; today is marked; a bad date or view falls back to today's day view; empty-state wording.
- `tests/e2e/test_my_bookings.py` -- at both widths: book for tomorrow, open My bookings, go to the week view, see today marked and the booking listed, open it and land on its details.
- `README.md` -- mention My bookings.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given Hannah organises one booking and is an attendee of another, when she opens My bookings for that day, then both appear with room, time, title and "Organiser" / "Attending", and a booking she neither organises nor attends does not.
- Given any date, when the week view is shown, then it covers Monday to Sunday of that date's week, and Previous / Next move by exactly one week (one day in day view).
- Given today is in the view, when the page renders, then today's heading says "Today" and is marked `aria-current="date"`.
- Given a booking in the calendar, when it is clicked, then its details page opens.
- Given a 390px-wide screen, when the week view is shown, then the days are stacked lists, not side-by-side columns.

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `uv run pytest --ignore=tests/e2e` -- expected: all pass, including `tests/test_calendar.py`
- `uv run pytest tests/e2e` -- expected: all pass at laptop and phone widths, including `test_my_bookings.py`

+"""The only place that converts between UTC and UK time (AD-5).
+
+Services work in aware UTC datetimes; the database holds UTC text
+`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z`; the web layer turns UK dates and clock times into UTC with
+`uk_to_utc` and back for display with the Jinja filters `clock` and `day`.
+"""
+
+from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time, timedelta
+from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
+
+UK = ZoneInfo("Europe/London")
+UTC_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:00Z"
+
+
+def utc_now() -> datetime:
+    """Now, in UTC. Tests replace this to fix the clock."""
+    return datetime.now(UTC)
+
+
+def to_text(moment: datetime) -> str:
+    return moment.astimezone(UTC).strftime(UTC_FORMAT)
+
+
+def from_text(text: str) -> datetime:
+    return datetime.strptime(text, UTC_FORMAT).replace(tzinfo=UTC)
+
+
+def uk_now() -> datetime:
+    return utc_now().astimezone(UK)
+
+
+def parse_date(text: str) -> date | None:
+    try:
+        return date.fromisoformat(text.strip())
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def parse_clock(text: str) -> time | None:
+    text = text.strip()
+    if len(text) != 5 or text[2] != ":":
+        return None
+    try:
+        return time.fromisoformat(text)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def uk_to_utc(day: date, clock: time) -> datetime | None:
+    """The UTC moment of a UK date and clock time, or None when the clocks skip it.
+
+    In the autumn hour that happens twice, the first (summer time) one is meant.
+    """
+    local = datetime.combine(day, clock).replace(tzinfo=UK, fold=0)
+    moment = local.astimezone(UTC)
+    if moment.astimezone(UK).replace(tzinfo=None) != local.replace(tzinfo=None):
+        return None
+    return moment
+
+
+def uk_midnight(day: date) -> datetime:
+    """The UTC moment a UK day starts. UK clocks change at 01:00 or 02:00, so midnight
+    always exists and happens once."""
+    return datetime.combine(day, time()).replace(tzinfo=UK).astimezone(UTC)
+
+
+def week_start(day: date) -> date:
+    """The Monday of `day`'s week."""
+    return day - timedelta(days=day.weekday())
+
+
+def next_quarter_hour(moment: datetime) -> datetime:
+    """`moment` rounded up to a quarter hour (unchanged when it is on one)."""
+    moment = moment.replace(second=0, microsecond=0) + (
+        timedelta(minutes=1) if moment.second or moment.microsecond else timedelta()
+    )
+    return moment + timedelta(minutes=-moment.minute % 15)
+
+
+def clock(moment: datetime) -> str:
+    """`14:00`, in UK time."""
+    return moment.astimezone(UK).strftime("%H:%M")
+
+
+def day(moment: datetime) -> str:
+    """`Tue 17 Nov`, in UK time."""
+    local = moment.astimezone(UK)
+    return f"{local:%a} {local.day} {local:%b}"
+
+
+def length_label(minutes: int) -> str:
+    """`15 min`, `1 h`, `1 h 45 min`."""
+    hours, rest = divmod(minutes, 60)
+    parts = ([f"{hours} h"] if hours else []) + ([f"{rest} min"] if rest else [])
+    return " ".join(parts)

"""Tables and queries for `bookings` and `booking_attendees`.

Imported only by `bookings.service` (AD-1, AD-3). The tables and the AD-4 triggers are
created by Alembic (AD-10); these definitions describe them for queries. Times are UTC
text `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z`, so text order is time order (AD-5).
"""

from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence

from sqlalchemy import Column, ForeignKey, Integer, MetaData, Row, String, Table, delete, select
from sqlalchemy import insert as sa_insert
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

metadata = MetaData()

bookings = Table(
    "bookings",
    metadata,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column("room_id", Integer, nullable=False),  # FK to rooms.id in the database
    Column("organiser_id", Integer, nullable=False),  # FK to people.id in the database
    Column("title", String, nullable=False),
    Column("start_at", String, nullable=False),
    Column("end_at", String, nullable=False),
)

booking_attendees = Table(
    "booking_attendees",
    metadata,
    Column("booking_id", Integer, ForeignKey("bookings.id"), primary_key=True),
    Column("person_id", Integer, primary_key=True),  # FK to people.id in the database
)


def begin_immediate(session: Session) -> None:
    """Start a write transaction that holds SQLite's write lock from the start (AD-4).

    The driver opens no transaction for reads, so after ending the session's current
    one there is none open and an explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE is allowed.
    """
    session.commit()
    session.connection().exec_driver_sql("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")


def overlapping(session: Session, start_at: str, end_at: str) -> Sequence[Row]:
    """Bookings in any room that overlap [start_at, end_at), in start order."""
    return session.execute(
        select(bookings)
        .where(bookings.c.start_at < end_at, bookings.c.end_at > start_at)
        .order_by(bookings.c.start_at, bookings.c.id)
    ).all()


def upcoming_for_organiser(
    session: Session, organiser_id: int, after: str, limit: int
) -> Sequence[Row]:
    """The organiser's bookings that end after `after`, soonest first."""
    return session.execute(
        select(bookings)
        .where(bookings.c.organiser_id == organiser_id, bookings.c.end_at > after)
        .order_by(bookings.c.start_at, bookings.c.id)
        .limit(limit)
    ).all()


def get(session: Session, booking_id: int) -> Row | None:
    return session.execute(select(bookings).where(bookings.c.id == booking_id)).first()


def attendee_ids(session: Session, booking_id: int) -> list[int]:
    rows = session.execute(
        select(booking_attendees.c.person_id).where(booking_attendees.c.booking_id == booking_id)
    )
    return [row.person_id for row in rows]


def insert(
    session: Session,
    room_id: int,
    organiser_id: int,
    title: str,
    start_at: str,
    end_at: str,
    attendees: Iterable[int],
) -> int:
    booking_id = session.execute(
        sa_insert(bookings).values(
            room_id=room_id,
            organiser_id=organiser_id,
            title=title,
            start_at=start_at,
            end_at=end_at,
        )
    ).inserted_primary_key[0]
    rows = [{"booking_id": booking_id, "person_id": person_id} for person_id in attendees]
    if rows:
        session.execute(sa_insert(booking_attendees), rows)
    return booking_id


def delete_booking(session: Session, booking_id: int) -> None:
    """Delete a booking; its attendees go with it (ON DELETE CASCADE, AD-13)."""
    session.execute(delete(bookings).where(bookings.c.id == booking_id))

"""My bookings: the current person's bookings by day and by week, today highlighted.

Calls `calendar.service` only (AD-1), and `core.time` for UK days (AD-5). Navigation is
plain links, so every view is a full page load (AD-2).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta
from typing import Annotated
from urllib.parse import urlencode

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request
from fastapi.responses import Response
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from roombooker.bookings.service import BookingView
from roombooker.calendar import service
from roombooker.core import time as uk
from roombooker.core.db import get_session
from roombooker.core.identity import CurrentPerson

router = APIRouter()

DbSession = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]

VIEWS = ("day", "week")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Day:
    date: date
    label: str
    is_today: bool
    bookings: tuple[BookingView, ...]


def _url(view: str, day: date) -> str:
    return "/my-bookings?" + urlencode({"view": view, "date": day.isoformat()})


def _label(day: date) -> str:
    """`Tue 17 Nov`, from a UK date."""
    return f"{day:%a} {day.day} {day:%b}"


def _empty_text(view: str, first: date, today: date) -> str:
    if view == "day":
        return "No bookings today." if first == today else f"No bookings on {_label(first)}."
    if first <= today < first + timedelta(days=7):
        return "No bookings this week."
    return f"No bookings in the week of {_label(first)}."


@router.api_route("/my-bookings", methods=["GET", "HEAD"])
def my_bookings(
    request: Request,
    session: DbSession,
    person: CurrentPerson,
    view: str = "day",
    date: str = "",
) -> Response:
    today = uk.uk_now().date()
    view = view if view in VIEWS else "day"
    chosen = uk.parse_date(date) or today
    first = uk.week_start(chosen) if view == "week" else chosen
    count = 7 if view == "week" else 1
    dates = [first + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(count)]
    bounds = [uk.uk_midnight(d) for d in [*dates, dates[-1] + timedelta(days=1)]]
    bookings = service.my_bookings(session, person, bounds[0], bounds[-1])
    days = [
        Day(
            date=d,
            label=_label(d),
            is_today=d == today,
            bookings=tuple(b for b in bookings if b.start_at < bounds[i + 1] and b.end_at > bounds[i]),
        )
        for i, d in enumerate(dates)
    ]
    step = timedelta(days=count)
    if view == "week":
        heading = f"Week of {_label(first)}"
    else:
        heading = f"Today, {_label(first)}" if first == today else _label(first)
    return request.app.state.templates.TemplateResponse(
        request,
        "calendar/my_bookings.html",
        {
            "person": person,
            "view": view,
            "heading": heading,
            "days": days,
            "is_empty": not bookings,
            "empty_text": _empty_text(view, first, today),
            "day_url": _url("day", chosen),
            "week_url": _url("week", chosen),
            "previous_url": _url(view, chosen - step),
            "next_url": _url(view, chosen + step),
            "today_url": _url(view, today),
            "previous_label": "Previous week" if view == "week" else "Previous day",
            "next_label": "Next week" if view == "week" else "Next day",
        },
    )

"""My bookings: today marked, a booking opens its details; week columns on a laptop and
day-headed lists on a phone."""

import re
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta

import httpx
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect

from roombooker.core import time as uk
from tests.e2e.conftest import pick


def test_week_view_lists_your_booking_and_opens_it(page: Page, live_server, viewport):
    room, title = f"Nook {uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}", f"Retro {uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    ids = live_server.person_ids()
    anna, hannah = ids["anna.kowalski@example.com"][0], ids["hannah.okafor@example.com"][0]
    today = uk.uk_now().date()
    tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
    with httpx.Client(base_url=live_server.url, cookies={"person_id": str(anna)}) as client:
        assert client.post("/manage-rooms", data={"name": room, "capacity": "4"}).status_code == 303
        page_html = client.get("/rooms", params={"date": tomorrow.isoformat()}).text
        room_id = re.search(rf'room=(\d+)&[^"]*">Book<span class="visually-hidden"> {room},', page_html)[1]
        booked = client.post(
            "/bookings",
            data={
                "room": room_id,
                "date": tomorrow.isoformat(),
                "start": "14:00",
                "length": "60",
                "title": title,
                "attendee_id": str(hannah),
            },
        )
        assert booked.status_code == 303

    page.goto("/")
    pick(page, "okaf", "Hannah Okafor")
    page.get_by_role("link", name="My bookings").click()
    page.get_by_role("link", name="Week", exact=True).click()

    today_heading = page.locator('[aria-current="date"]')
    expect(today_heading).to_have_text(re.compile(r"^Today, "))
    if uk.week_start(tomorrow) != uk.week_start(today):
        page.get_by_role("link", name="Next week").click()

    days = page.locator(".calendar-day")
    expect(days).to_have_count(7)
    first, second = days.nth(0).bounding_box(), days.nth(1).bounding_box()
    if viewport["width"] >= 768:
        assert first["y"] == second["y"] and second["x"] > first["x"]  # columns
    else:
        assert second["y"] > first["y"] and second["x"] == first["x"]  # stacked lists

    booking = page.get_by_role("link", name=re.compile(rf"14:00–15:00 {title} {room}, London Attending"))
    expect(booking).to_be_visible()
    booking.click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name=title)).to_be_visible()
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/bookings/\d+$"))

"""My bookings: today marked, a booking opens its details; week columns on a laptop and
day-headed lists on a phone."""

import re
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta

import httpx
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect

from roombooker.core import time as uk
from tests.e2e.conftest import pick


def test_week_view_lists_your_booking_and_opens_it(page: Page, live_server, viewport):
    room, title = f"Nook {uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}", f"Retro {uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    ids = live_server.person_ids()
    anna, hannah = ids["anna.kowalski@example.com"][0], ids["hannah.okafor@example.com"][0]
    today = uk.uk_now().date()
    tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
    with httpx.Client(base_url=live_server.url, cookies={"person_id": str(anna)}) as client:
        assert client.post("/manage-rooms", data={"name": room, "capacity": "4"}).status_code == 303
        page_html = client.get("/rooms", params={"date": tomorrow.isoformat()}).text
        room_id = re.search(rf'room=(\d+)&[^"]*">Book<span class="visually-hidden"> {room},', page_html)[1]
        booked = client.post(
            "/bookings",
            data={
                "room": room_id,
                "date": tomorrow.isoformat(),
                "start": "14:00",
                "length": "60",
                "title": title,
                "attendee_id": str(hannah),
            },
        )
        assert booked.status_code == 303

    page.goto("/")
    pick(page, "okaf", "Hannah Okafor")
    page.get_by_role("link", name="My bookings").click()
    page.get_by_role("link", name="Week", exact=True).click()

    today_heading = page.locator('[aria-current="date"]')
    expect(today_heading).to_have_text(re.compile(r"^Today, "))
    if uk.week_start(tomorrow) != uk.week_start(today):
        page.get_by_role("link", name="Next week").click()

    days = page.locator(".calendar-day")
    expect(days).to_have_count(7)
    first, second = days.nth(0).bounding_box(), days.nth(1).bounding_box()
    if viewport["width"] >= 768:
        assert first["y"] == second["y"] and second["x"] > first["x"]  # columns
    else:
        assert second["y"] > first["y"] and second["x"] == first["x"]  # stacked lists

    booking = page.get_by_role("link", name=re.compile(rf"14:00–15:00 {title} {room}, London Attending"))
    expect(booking).to_be_visible()
    booking.click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name=title)).to_be_visible()
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/bookings/\d+$"))

from roombooker.core import time as uk

db, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
base = "http://127.0.0.1:8765"
ids = {e: i for i, e in sqlite3.connect(db).execute("select id, email from people")}
anna, hannah = ids["anna.kowalski@example.com"], ids["hannah.okafor@example.com"]
c = httpx.Client(base_url=base, cookies={"person_id": str(anna)})
for n in ("Board", "Snug"):
    c.post("/manage-rooms", data={"name": n, "capacity": "8"})
rooms = {n: i for i, n in sqlite3.connect(db).execute("select id, name from rooms")}
today = uk.uk_now().date()
for d, s, r, t, who in [
    (1, "09:00", "Board", "Weekly planning", hannah),
    (1, "14:00", "Snug", "Design review", anna),
    (2, "11:30", "Board", "1:1 with Ben", hannah),
]:
    cl = httpx.Client(base_url=base, cookies={"person_id": str(who)})
    r = cl.post("/bookings", data={"room": rooms[r], "date": (today + timedelta(days=d)).isoformat(),
                                   "start": s, "length": "60", "title": t, "attendee_id": str(hannah)})
    print(r.status_code)
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()
    for name, vp in [("laptop", {"width": 1280, "height": 800}), ("phone", {"width": 390, "height": 844})]:
        ctx = b.new_context(viewport=vp, base_url=base)
        ctx.add_cookies([{"name": "person_id", "value": str(hannah), "url": base}])
        pg = ctx.new_page()
        pg.goto("/my-bookings?view=week")
        pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}/{name}-week.png", full_page=True)
        pg.goto(f"/my-bookings?date={(today + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()}")
        pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}/{name}-day.png", full_page=True)
    b.close()

# room-booker

Company Room Booking: internal room booking for the London, Manchester and Leeds offices.
One FastAPI app, one SQLite file, server-rendered pages with htmx.

## First local run

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). It installs Python 3.14 for you if it is missing.

Run these from the repository root, in order:

```sh
uv sync                                                  # install Python 3.14 and dependencies
uv run alembic upgrade head                              # create the database in var/roombooker.db
uv run python -m roombooker.seed seeds/build-people.csv  # load the made-up offices and people
uv run uvicorn roombooker.app:app                        # serve the app
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/>. You land on Pick your name; type part of a name and pick it.
Your name then shows in the top bar; tap it to switch to someone else.
You land on Rooms: pick a date, start time and length (15 minutes to 4 hours) to see the free rooms,
your own office first, and book one with a title and attendees. Open a booking to see it; the person
who booked it can cancel it. Bookings can't overlap, start in the past or start more than 90 days ahead.
Office managers land on Manage rooms, where they add, edit, close and reopen their office's rooms.
Closing a room cancels its bookings that have not started yet.

# room-booker

Company Room Booking: internal room booking for the London, Manchester and Leeds offices.
One FastAPI app, one SQLite file, server-rendered pages with htmx.

## First local run

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). It installs Python 3.14 for you if it is missing.

Run these from the repository root, in order:

```sh
uv sync                                                  # install Python 3.14 and dependencies
uv run alembic upgrade head                              # create the database in var/roombooker.db
uv run python -m roombooker.seed seeds/build-people.csv  # load the made-up offices and people
uv run uvicorn roombooker.app:app                        # serve the app
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/>. You land on Pick your name; type part of a name and pick it.
Your name then shows in the top bar; tap it to switch to someone else.
You land on Rooms: pick a date, start time and length (15 minutes to 4 hours) to see the free rooms,
your own office first, and book one with a title and attendees. Open a booking to see it; the person
who booked it can cancel it. Bookings can't overlap, start in the past or start more than 90 days ahead.
Office managers land on Manage rooms, where they add, edit, close and reopen their office's rooms.
Closing a room cancels its bookings that have not started yet.

## Loading people

The same command loads the build seed and HR's list:

```sh
uv run python -m roombooker.seed path/to/people.csv
```

The CSV has the columns `email,name,office,office_manager`. Offices are created by name.
`office_manager` is `true`, `yes` or `1` for an office manager, and `false`, `no`, `0` or blank otherwise.
People are matched on email: a reload updates them in place, and anyone missing from the file is
marked inactive (never deleted), so everyone keeps their id. If any row is wrong, nothing is loaded
and the command exits non-zero, naming the line and the problem.

## Settings

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ROOMBOOKER_DB_PATH` | `var/roombooker.db` | SQLite file; its folder is created if missing |
| `ROOMBOOKER_ENV` | `local` | `production` marks the name cookie `Secure` (HTTPS only) |

## Tests

```sh
uv run playwright install chromium   # once, for the browser tests
uv run pytest                        # all tests, including browser tests at laptop and phone widths
uv run pytest --ignore=tests/e2e     # without the browser tests
```

## Schema changes

Every table change is an Alembic migration in `migrations/versions/`; run `uv run alembic upgrade head`
before starting the app.

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** People can book rooms, but the only place they see their bookings is the "Your upcoming bookings" list on Rooms. That list shows only bookings they organise, not ones they were invited to, and they can't look at a given day or week. This is loose work outside the initiative tree (user, 2026-11-12), built as asked rather than as `epic-my-calendar`.

**Approach:** Add a My bookings page with a day view and a week view of every booking the current person organises or attends. Today is highlighted. Each booking shows its room, time and title and links to its details page. On a phone the same bookings show as a list.

</frozen-after-approval>

## Implementation Notes

Oneshot route, pinned by the workflow. The work is read-only (no new table, no write path, no rule change), so risk is low. The architecture spine already names the module (`calendar`, web and service, no store, AD-1/AD-3) and the route (`/my-bookings`). Decisions:

- `bookings.store.for_person(session, person_id, start, end)` finds bookings that overlap `[start, end)` where the person is the organiser or in `booking_attendees`, in start order. `bookings.service.bookings_for_person(session, viewer, start_at, end_at)` returns them as `BookingView`s through `_views` (AD-3, AD-8). `calendar.service.my_bookings` is the only thing `calendar.web` calls, and it calls only `bookings.service` (AD-1).
